descriptions.text: Valtay Corporation Neural Enhancer #544. Variant 32.c This item is compatible with your Morphology and Interface. Warning: This pill will cause a permanent change to your brain. This item cannot be unequipped or undone once installed. Warning: You do not have a Valtay Corporation Neural Interface installed. While your current wetware system is compatible with this Neural Enhancer, it is recommended you visit a Valtay Corporate Outreach Center to discuss upgrade options. Payment and Legacy plans available. Keeping the Best of You alive. Current wetware: Syndicate Crawl Version 47.002.Human. Taking this pill will install the following upgrade to your interface: Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals.

beats.headline: A pill from the worms
beats.text: Donut is sure Princess D'nadia has got her something good, and makes Carl open the bronze benefactor box he has just received, and send a thank-you. Sparks fly as it opens. On its top is a circle with a squiggle through it, and etched underneath, The Valtay Corporation, Keeping the Best of You Alive. Carl shivers, remembering what the Valtay really are. Inside is a single blue and yellow capsule, and for a terrifying moment he thinks it is an actual brain worm. Its description is in a slightly different voice and font than usual, and it offers one upgrade: Identify and Analyze Subspace Portals.

beats.headline: Down with cold coffee
beats.text: Why him, Carl wonders, and why the hurry, and can he trust a description in a different format? He puts it in his inventory first and notes its value, just below the Kimaris figure, and its rarity, common, then pulls it back out, reasonably certain the inventory would have refused a hidden parasite. Then he swallows it with his cold cup of coffee. A new tab appears, Third-Party Upgrades, warning that communication-based upgrades are disabled in the dungeon; the neural enhancer is its only item, and clicking it says only: This upgrade is working properly. He thanks his sponsor in the notes without knowing what it does.

beats.headline: The door glows purple
beats.text: Carl is about to follow Katia to the training room when his eyes catch the doorway out to the coffee shop. It glows purple now, and a tooltip calls it a Standard Subspace Portal. Analyze? A page of numbers he cannot make sense of, and at the bottom the lines that matter: two-way, gated to user, he can pass, the environment beyond is compatible. Visual Analysis? Yes. A still photo of the coffee shop pops up, empty of customers, with Nodd the Bopca behind the counter picking his nose.

beats.headline: A yard full of engines
beats.text: At Abyss Station a driverless train nosedives into the pit, and Carl looks up at the portal over it: an Ultima Corp DungeonWerx Industrial Subspace Portal. The analysis runs much longer than the last one. He is facing the wrong side, and entering from it will do nothing. Passage is gated by conveyance type and to key holders, with compatible keys marked in his inventory. Visual Analysis shows a massive trainyard, thousands of trains spreading out in all directions, only the engine cars, all inside a high fence.

beats.headline: Half a mile over the pit
beats.text: In station 75's yard Carl reads the portals. The first of four multi-destination light-duty ones, each signed with forty-eight coloured lines, needs a selector to dial and defaults to the Orange Line; its picture is just a stretch of track. The heavy-duty clean-up portal at the front of a rapid-response cart is set to the abyss and carries an environmental warning, and the picture shows why: whatever it catches comes out in the air over the pit, a good half mile above the ground. Elevation is the highlighted problem. He switches the selector to the trainyard, and the warning goes away.

beats.headline: The right one
beats.text: Prepotente explains the portal dial, Carl calls out the numbers Rosetta gives him, and he analyses the door: an Ultima Corp DungeonWerx Municipal, Multi-Destination Doorway-based Subspace Portal. Dial 453! The information changes: two-way, gated by faith, its entrance sequence gated to adherents of the Khepri faith or other entities under the dungeon's ruleset. That's the right one, Carl calls. He holds his breath and asks for the picture. A screenshot appears, and relief floods him.

beats.headline: Incompatibility mode
beats.text: Carl examines the portal with his neural implant, and it warns him first: it is working in incompatibility mode due to recent changes to his wetware system, and he should see his Valtay representative for repair. Only limited details are available. Unknown Manufacturer Enhancement Zone Subspace Portal. One-way, open access, and it leads to a stasis chamber. Visual Analysis: unavailable. Carl wags his tail; it is pretty much what he was hoping it would say. Hopefully the implant will go back to working properly when he stops being a damn dog.
